title: MV Massive error after transferring game project to a new computer

posts.author: muffinswords
posts.body:
I recently came into a new computer and put RPG Maker MV on it, then transferred a copy of my project too.
At first glance, everything seemed to be working fine. But upon transferring to a map that made use of Galv's Layer Graphics and show pictures (those were what happened in the only event on the map), I ran into an error that was not present on my old computer.
The screen is also completely black when it was fine on the other laptop.

posts.author: muffinswords
posts.body: I ran a test and found out that a smaller size layer loads correctly on a different map. It might have to do with it being a very large layer? Yet it was okay on my old laptop. I went ahead and asked on Galv's site too. And I'll make sure to get the latest files.

posts.author: Galv
posts.body:
If you are using huge layers (which I do not recommend you do), that could be the cause.
Doing some research, the maximum image size WebGL can draw is dependent on GPU and browser, but a common hardware-supported limit is 4096×4096 pixels.

Thanks for replying. I love your Layer Graphics plugin!
Big maps are important to me, and I wonder why it was working on a laptop that was older while this is a gaming pc with a good GPU and CPU.
That being said, if players would end up having technical problems with huge maps, I don't want that. I tried cutting the test map in half, to a 100x100 map with a 4800x4800 layer. It worked!
I then tried it as 150x150 with 7200x7200. It still works!
But I am wary that as you say, the common limit is 4096. I want most players to be able to play. Another problem is that the (7200) layer is almost 100MB! The 200x200 map I was testing must have had that layer be MORE than 100MB. My project would have become ridiculously HUGE. No wonder big layers cause problems.
Are there any alternatives for having nicer big maps? I am considering Yanfly Grid Free Doodads as an option. Also considering making many smaller (100x100) maps with layer graphics and linking them together somehow.

posts.author: Galv
posts.body: Those sound like good options. In the layer graphics plugin you can create smaller static layers set to x,y positions so could make your map from smaller layers and only load them as needed depending on player position. That would be more complex setup, though. I would recommend smaller maps and more optimized layer graphics (png files increase more in file size with things like gradient transparencies and different colors they have).

The problem with that idea is that it's only the filesize on HDD that gets compressed. That helps with download sizes, but nothing else.
A picture in RAM needs to be uncompressed to be worked with, so all your compression utilities for the filesize do nothing for the RAM limits themselves.
